about: Generated by scripts/snapshot_discovery_source_types.py from the Platform's discovery source types; do not edit by hand, except the entries for vendors only a standalone engine has.

fields.name: regions
fields.description: Required. AWS regions to read, comma-separated. Example: us-east-1,us-west-2

fields.name: list_agents
fields.description: List Bedrock agents and AgentCore runtimes. Needs bedrock:ListAgents and bedrock-agentcore:ListAgentRuntimes. Defaults to true.

fields.name: read_cloudtrail
fields.description: Also find workloads that call Bedrock models directly, from CloudTrail management events: one agent per calling IAM role. Needs cloudtrail:LookupEvents; no trail setup. Calls made through SSO roles are people and are not reported. Defaults to true.

fields.name: role_arn
fields.description: IAM role to assume before reading, for another account or a credential that holds no Bedrock permissions itself. Example: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/arthur-discovery

fields.name: external_id
fields.description: External ID the role's trust policy requires, sent when assuming role_arn.

fields.name: access_key_id
fields.description: IAM access key ID, set together with secret_access_key. Leave both empty only when the engine is configured to use its own AWS credentials.

fields.name: secret_access_key
fields.description: Secret of the IAM access key.

fields.name: regions
fields.description: AWS regions whose ECS clusters and EKS clusters are listed, and whose CloudTrail is read, comma-separated. Example: us-east-1,us-west-2

fields.name: read_cloudtrail
fields.description: Report a workload whose IAM role CloudTrail shows calling Bedrock models, with the models it called. Needs cloudtrail:LookupEvents; no trail setup. Defaults to true.

fields.name: report_all_workloads
fields.description: Report every workload with the IAM role it runs as, not only those whose image is a known agent's or whose role calls Bedrock. Defaults to false.

fields.name: role_arn
fields.description: IAM role to assume before reading, for another account or a credential that holds no permissions itself. Example: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/arthur-discovery. The role (or the key's user) needs these read-only actions: ecs:ListClusters, ecs:ListServices, ecs:DescribeServices, ecs:ListTasks, ecs:DescribeTasks, ecs:DescribeTaskDefinition, ecs:DescribeContainerInstances, ec2:DescribeInstances, iam:GetInstanceProfile, eks:ListClusters, eks:DescribeCluster, eks:ListNodegroups, eks:DescribeNodegroup, eks:ListPodIdentityAssociations, eks:DescribePodIdentityAssociation, eks:ListFargateProfiles, eks:DescribeFargateProfile, and cloudtrail:LookupEvents. On each EKS cluster it also needs an access entry with AmazonEKSViewPolicy at cluster scope.

fields.name: external_id
fields.description: External ID the role's trust policy requires, sent when assuming role_arn.

fields.name: access_key_id
fields.description: IAM access key ID, set together with secret_access_key. Leave both empty only when the engine is configured to use its own AWS credentials.

fields.name: secret_access_key
fields.description: Secret of the IAM access key.

fields.name: regions
fields.description: AWS regions whose EC2 instances are read, as comma-separated region names, or all for every region each account has enabled. Every instance in them is listed, so an instance the collector was never deployed to is counted rather than missed. Example: us-east-1, eu-west-1

fields.name: accounts
fields.description: AWS accounts to read, each through its member role (member_role_name): all for every active account in the organization, or comma-separated 12-digit account IDs. Empty reads only the credential's own account. The credential then needs sts:AssumeRole on the member roles, and organizations:ListAccounts for all, from the management account or a delegated administrator. An account whose role cannot be assumed is reported as a denied scope and the rest are read. Example: all

fields.name: include_tags
fields.description: Instance tags to scan, as comma-separated key=value pairs, matched exactly and case-sensitively. An instance carrying any of them is scanned. Empty scans every instance in the regions. A pair no instance carries is reported with a count of 0; a pair that is not key=value fails the scan. A tag whose key holds '=' or ',' cannot be written here. Example: env=prod, team=ml

fields.name: exclude_tags
fields.description: Instance tags never to scan, as comma-separated key=value pairs. Wins over include_tags: an instance carrying one is left out, and nothing from it is read or reported. A pair that is not key=value fails the scan. Example: env=dev

fields.name: role_arn
fields.description: ARN of a role in the account to assume for the scan. Grant it ec2:DescribeInstances, ssm:DescribeInstanceInformation and ssm:ListInventoryEntries, plus ec2:DescribeRegions when regions is all, and nothing more. Leave empty to scan with the access key itself, which then needs the same actions. Not needed with accounts, where each member role holds them. Example: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/arthur-discovery

fields.name: external_id
fields.description: External ID the role's trust policy requires, if any. Sent when assuming role_arn, or, with accounts, each account's member role.

fields.name: member_role_name
fields.description: Name of the role read in each account when accounts is set: a role name, not an ARN. It holds the same actions as role_arn, plus ec2:DescribeRegions. Empty means arthur-ai-discovery, the name the endpoint AI discovery CloudFormation template gives it.

fields.name: access_key_id
fields.description: Access key ID to scan with, or to assume role_arn with. Leave empty only when the engine is configured to use its own AWS credentials.

fields.name: secret_access_key
fields.description: Secret access key for access_key_id.

fields.name: region
fields.description: AWS region of the CloudWatch Logs log groups. Example: us-east-1

fields.name: log_group_names
fields.description: CloudWatch Logs log groups holding the network logs, comma-separated, up to 20. A log group shared into a monitoring account is given by its ARN. Example: /aws/route53resolver/prod-vpc

fields.name: log_format
fields.description: How the log lines are read: route53_resolver_query_log (Route 53 Resolver query logs), vpc_flow_log_v2 (VPC Flow Logs, default format), or custom to use extraction_regex. Flow logs carry only IP addresses, so they match only the ranges in extra_inference_hosts.

fields.name: extraction_regex
fields.description: Required when log_format is custom, and read only then: a regex with named groups. src (the internal source) and dest (the hostname or IP it called) are required; instance_id, interface_id, vpc_id, account_id and timestamp are optional, but a line needs instance_id, interface_id or vpc_id to be placed, since one address in two VPCs is two hosts. (?<name>...) and (?P<name>...) both work. At most 2048 characters. Example: src=(?<src>\S+) vpc=(?<vpc_id>\S+) dst_host=(?<dest>\S+)

fields.name: access_key_id
fields.description: IAM access key ID, set together with secret_access_key. Leave both empty only when the engine is configured to use its own AWS credentials. Example: AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE

fields.name: secret_access_key
fields.description: Secret of the IAM access key. The credential needs only logs:FilterLogEvents on the log groups (and sts:AssumeRole on role_arn when one is set).

fields.name: role_arn
fields.description: IAM role to assume before reading, for log groups in another account or a credential that holds no log permissions itself. Example: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/arthur-discovery

fields.name: external_id
fields.description: External ID the role's trust policy requires, sent when assuming role_arn.

fields.name: extra_inference_hosts
fields.description: Destinations to treat as inference endpoints in addition to the built-in list of model providers, comma-separated, up to 100: hosts (a host also matches its subdomains; * stands for part of one label) or IP addresses and CIDR ranges. Example: llm-gateway.example.com, 10.50.0.0/16

fields.name: project_endpoint
fields.description: Endpoint of the Azure AI Foundry project whose agents are listed, from the project's overview page. Example: https://my-resource.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/my-project

fields.name: tenant_id
fields.description: Microsoft Entra tenant ID of the service principal the engine reads with. Leave empty when the engine uses its own Azure identity. Example: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: Application (client) ID of the service principal the engine reads with. Leave empty when the engine uses its own Azure identity.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: Client secret of the service principal. The principal needs a role on the project that can read its agents, such as Azure AI User. Leave empty only when the engine runs with its own Azure identity, which then needs the same role.

fields.name: elasticsearch_url
fields.description: Elasticsearch endpoint of the cluster holding the logs - not the Kibana URL. Must be https. Elasticsearch 8.14 or later. Examples: https://my-deployment.es.us-east-1.aws.elastic.cloud, https://elasticsearch.internal.example.com:9200

fields.name: api_key
fields.description: Encoded value of an Elasticsearch API key whose role descriptors grant 'read' on the indices the query reads; no cluster privilege is needed. Not an Elastic Cloud organization API key, which cannot query a cluster. Give the key an expiration: Elasticsearch keys never expire by default.

fields.name: ca_certificate
fields.description: PEM certificate of the CA that signed the cluster's HTTP certificate, when it is a private CA. For a self-managed cluster with auto-configured security this is config/certs/http_ca.crt. Required when tls_verification is ca_only. Otherwise, empty trusts the engine's system CAs, which is right for Elastic Cloud.

fields.name: tls_verification
fields.description: How the cluster's certificate is checked. full (the default): issuer and hostname. ca_only: issuer only, trusting just the CA in ca_certificate, for a certificate that does not name the host the engine connects to; needs ca_certificate. off: no check at all.

fields.name: project_ids
fields.description: IDs of the GCP projects whose Compute Engine VMs are read, as comma-separated project IDs. Every VM in them is listed, so a VM the collector was never deployed to is counted rather than missed. Set this, organization_id or folder_ids. Example: prod-apps-123456, data-platform-654321

fields.name: organization_id
fields.description: The organization's number: every active project under it is read, its folders walked. Needs roles/browser and roles/compute.viewer granted on the organization. Example: 123456789012

fields.name: folder_ids
fields.description: Comma-separated folder numbers: every active project under each is read. Needs roles/browser and roles/compute.viewer granted on the folders. Example: 111111111111, 222222222222

fields.name: include_labels
fields.description: VM labels to scan, as comma-separated key=value pairs. A VM carrying any of them is scanned. Empty scans every VM in the projects. A pair no VM carries is reported with a count of 0; a pair that is not key=value fails the scan. Example: env=prod, team=ml

fields.name: exclude_labels
fields.description: VM labels never to scan, as comma-separated key=value pairs. Wins over include_labels: a VM carrying one is left out, and nothing from it is read or reported. A pair that is not key=value fails the scan. Example: env=dev

fields.name: service_account_key
fields.description: JSON key of a service account that can list the projects' VMs and read their guest attributes (roles/compute.viewer is sufficient; a custom role needs compute.instances.list, compute.instances.getGuestAttributes and compute.projects.get). Paste the whole key file. Leave empty only when the engine is configured to use its own workload credentials.

fields.name: project_ids
fields.description: IDs (not numbers) of the GCP projects whose Cloud Run services, Cloud Run jobs and GKE workloads are listed, comma-separated. Example: my-project-123456

fields.name: regions
fields.description: Regions to list Cloud Run jobs in, comma-separated. Empty asks every region Cloud Run serves, one call each, which takes most of a scan's time. Example: us-central1,us-east4

fields.name: report_all_workloads
fields.description: Report every workload with the service account it runs as, not only those whose image is a known agent's or whose own service account called a Vertex AI model. Defaults to false.

fields.name: service_account_key
fields.description: JSON key of a service account with roles/run.viewer and roles/container.viewer on each project, plus roles/logging.privateLogViewer to select workloads by the service accounts that called Vertex AI models (Data Access audit logs must be on for aiplatform.googleapis.com). Without it, workloads are selected by catalog image only and the audit log is reported as a denied scope. Paste the whole key file. Leave empty only when the engine is configured to use its own workload credentials.

fields.name: project_id
fields.description: ID of the GCP project whose Cloud DNS query logs and VPC flow logs are read. Under Shared VPC this is the host project. Cloud DNS logging (a DNS server policy on the VPC network) and subnet flow logs must be on. Example: my-project-123456

fields.name: service_account_key
fields.description: JSON key of a service account with roles/logging.viewer on the project; roles/run.viewer also lets Cloud Run job executions be reported as their job. Paste the whole key file. Leave empty only when the engine is configured to use its own workload credentials.

fields.name: extra_inference_hosts
fields.description: Destinations to treat as inference endpoints in addition to the built-in list of model providers, comma-separated, up to 100: hosts (a host also matches its subdomains; * stands for part of one label) or IP addresses and CIDR ranges. Example: llm-gateway.example.com, 10.50.0.0/16

fields.name: project_id
fields.description: ID of the GCP project whose Vertex AI Agent Engines (reasoning engines) are listed. Example: my-project-123456

fields.name: location
fields.description: Vertex AI region the Agent Engines are deployed in. Defaults to us-central1. Example: europe-west1

fields.name: service_account_key
fields.description: JSON key of the service account the engine reads with. roles/aiplatform.viewer lists Agent Engines; with read_audit_logs on, it also needs roles/logging.privateLogViewer. Paste the whole key file. Leave empty only when the engine is configured to use its own workload credentials, which then need the same roles.

fields.name: read_audit_logs
fields.description: Also find workloads (VMs, Cloud Run, GKE) that call Vertex AI models directly, from the project's Data Access audit log: one agent per calling service account. Needs Data Access audit logs enabled for aiplatform.googleapis.com, and roles/logging.privateLogViewer on the project for the account the engine reads with: the pasted key's service account, or the engine's own workload identity when no key is set. Without that role the scan still succeeds but finds no callers, and the job log says so. Defaults to false.

fields.name: base_url
fields.description: Base URL of the Jamf Pro tenant. Must be https - the token request carries the client secret in its body. Example: https://yourorg.jamfcloud.com

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: Client ID of a Jamf Pro API client whose role can read computer inventory. Sensitive because it is half of a credential pair, not because it addresses anything.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: Client secret paired with the client ID.

fields.name: include_groups
fields.description: Jamf Pro computer groups to scan, smart or static, as comma-separated names exactly as Jamf shows them. Empty scans every computer. A name Jamf does not have fails the scan. Needs the API client's role to hold Read Smart Computer Groups and Read Static Computer Groups. Example: Corp-Managed macOS, Engineering

fields.name: exclude_groups
fields.description: Jamf Pro computer groups never to scan, as comma-separated names. Wins over include_groups: a computer in both is left out, and nothing from it is decoded or reported. A name Jamf does not have fails the scan. Needs the same group privileges as include_groups. Example: Contractors, Executive Devices

fields.name: base_url
fields.description: Address of the LiteLLM proxy, the one its clients send requests to. Must be https. Example: https://litellm.example.com:4000

fields.name: api_key
fields.description: A LiteLLM key created for a user with the proxy_admin_viewer role, which can read the request log and the keys but change nothing. Not the master key.

fields.name: ca_certificate
fields.description: PEM certificate of the CA that signed the proxy's certificate, when it is a private CA. Required when tls_verification is ca_only. Otherwise, empty trusts the engine's system CAs.

fields.name: tls_verification
fields.description: How the proxy's certificate is checked. full (the default): issuer and hostname. ca_only: issuer only, trusting just the CA in ca_certificate, for a certificate that does not name the host the engine connects to; needs ca_certificate. off: no check at all.

fields.name: inventory_dir
fields.description: The folder, inside the engine's container, holding the endpoint collector's inventory.json for one machine. Deckard's scan-local.sh writes it.

fields.name: base_url
fields.description: Management port of a search head, or of the load balancer in front of a search head cluster - not an indexer, and not the HTTP Event Collector port (8088). Must be https. Examples: https://splunk.internal.example.com:8089, https://yourstack.splunkcloud.com:8089 (Splunk Cloud needs the engine's address on its search-api IP allow list)

fields.name: auth_token
fields.description: Splunk authentication token, from Settings > Tokens, for a user whose role can search the indexes the query reads. Not an HTTP Event Collector token, which can only send data in.

fields.name: ca_certificate
fields.description: PEM certificate of the CA that signed the management port's certificate, when it is a private CA. For an instance still on Splunk's default certificate this is $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/auth/cacert.pem. Required when tls_verification is ca_only. Otherwise, empty trusts the engine's system CAs.

fields.name: tls_verification
fields.description: How the management port's certificate is checked. full (the default): issuer and hostname. ca_only: issuer only, trusting just the CA in ca_certificate, for Splunk's default certificate, which names no host; needs ca_certificate. off: no check at all.

fields.name: team_id
fields.description: ID of the Vercel team to scan (Team Settings → General → Team ID), not the slug. Example: team_1a2b3c4d5e6f7g8h9i0j1k2l

fields.name: access_token
fields.description: Vercel access token scoped to the team. Arthur only reads: project metadata, environment variable names (never decrypted values), and deployed package.json files when Read deployment sources is on. Least privilege: on Enterprise, a member with the Enterprise Viewer role; on Pro, a Pro Viewer covers projects and deployments, but Observability Plus signals need a Member or Owner token.

fields.name: include_projects
fields.description: Comma-separated project names or IDs to limit the scan to. Leave empty to scan every project in the team. Example: support-bot,prj_abc123

fields.name: read_deployment_sources
fields.description: Off unless set to true. When on, Arthur reads package.json from each project's latest production deployment that was not built from Git (v0, CLI or API deployments) to detect AI libraries. This reads deployed source files, so it is opt-in.

fields.name: api_endpoint_url
fields.description: Your tenant's Wiz GraphQL API endpoint, shown in the Wiz console under User Settings → Tenant → API Endpoint URL. Must be https. Example: https://api.us17.app.wiz.io/graphql

fields.name: auth_environment
fields.description: The Wiz environment that issues your service account's tokens. commercial (most tenants): auth.app.wiz.io. gov: auth.gov.wiz.io. fedramp: auth.app.wiz.us.

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: Client ID of the Wiz service account Arthur reads the inventory with (Wiz console → Settings → Service Accounts).

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: Client secret of a Wiz service account (Settings > Service Accounts) with the read:resources and read:inventory scopes (read:all also works). Without read:inventory the scan still lists AI-SPM agents but skips workloads.

fields.name: entity_types
fields.description: Comma-separated Wiz Security Graph entity types to list as AI agents. Leave blank for AI_AGENT,AI_SERVICE. Other valid AI types include AI_AGENT_REGISTRY, AI_DEPLOYMENT, AI_GATEWAY, AI_MODEL, AI_TOOL and MCP_SERVER.
